'''Piame''', or '''Biami''', is a [[Sepik language]], which in 1988 was spoken in the village of Piame in northwestern [[Papua New Guinea]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Some language and sociolinguistic relationships - ProQuest |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1297882138 |access-date=2025-02-22 |website=www.proquest.com | id={{ProQuest|1297882138}} |language=en}}</ref>{{rp||page=249}}

== Relationship to other languages ==
Piame is closely related to [[Niksek language|Niksek]], with cognate percentages ranging from 44% to 53% for the different Niksek dialects.<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=249}}

== Sociolinguistics ==
In 1988, it was spoken by less than a hundred people, in the single village of Piame.<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=249}} The village was primarily [[Monolingualism|monolingual]]. Two or three men had begun to learn [[Tok Pisin]], the [[lingua franca]] of [[Papua New Guinea]].<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=254}}

The language is today described as [[Endangered language|moribund]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Piame |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/piam1243 |access-date=2025-02-22 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-06-03 |title=Piame {{!}} Ethnologue |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/pin/ |access-date=2025-02-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603190438/https://www.ethnologue.com/language/pin/ |archive-date=3 June 2013 }}</ref>
